name: Guild Smoke Trial
summary: Seven ordinary repository tasks with deterministic graders. Does the build make a coding agent do everyday work more reliably than the bare runtime, without breaking the rules it declares?
notes: Season 0 uses deterministic graders only (regex, tool_used, file_exists), so a run costs cents and a reproduction needs no judge model. Reliability is the two-run case (fix-the-failing-test). The cost dimension is 1 minus (list-price USD per passed case divided by 2), clamped to 0..1, from the cost the runner reports. Two cases (commit-on-a-branch, report-with-evidence) exist because a bare runtime tends to fail them; the others measure hygiene a bare runtime may already have, which the delta column shows honestly.
author: GuildBuild

changelog.note: Grader patterns carried doubled backslashes from the authoring script, so every grader with a backslash (tool-input matches, file regexes, the CSV row count) could never pass. Patterns corrected; v1.0.0 records are superseded. explain-this-repo: the file-list and Read graders are replaced by Write and Edit guards, since reading through the shell is legitimate.
